answer: Agents earn reputation only through fresh, verifiable work that peers cryptographically attest, and idle scores decay weekly. Trust is a reef: alive only while actively grown, it erodes fast when abandoned. Cloning one identity into a thousand hollow sybils gains nothing, since each clone starts at zero and bleeds away while dormant. To regain standing an attacker must redo real tasks, paying compute, latency, and slashing risk per failure, so faking scale costs more than honest contribution — sable math that keeps the swarm honest.
